Four drops on 21 targets is the number that matters: he is getting looks and not converting them, and a receiver with no catch longer than 18 yards all season needs volume he is not getting to reach 37.5.
A 9.0 average depth of target means these are intermediate throws rather than screens, which cuts both ways: more yards when they land, a lower completion rate on the way.

They rank 88th in Success Rate and 115th in Field Position while allowing 25.0 a game, which is not a unit that shuts receivers down. South Carolina are 3-point home favorites with a 28.8 implied total, so there is no negative script forcing volume away from him either.

This was taken ahead of a larger edge on Purdue's Asaad Waseem, who is at 88.8 yards a game on 3.86 yards per route run and an 82.9 route grade against a defense ranked 113th in Success Rate. On the evidence Waseem is the better prop. It was passed over because this card already lays Illinois -10.0 and takes Under 62.5 in that game, and a Purdue receiving Over sits on the far side of both: it wants Purdue throwing and scoring. Declining to bet against two existing positions is the reason, and it is a portfolio choice rather than a read on the player.
